story:
Eralyne was a student of the old schools in Avalon, young enough that she had not yet been given her own bench. On the night the colleges burned, when the readers were being put into the boats at the causeway, she went back into the burning school for something and came out with it under her cloak, and her robe on fire, and got onto the last boat to Caldey. She did not say what she had. She held it all the way across the water, and the boatmen say she was singing, the way the sorceresses sang their working-songs, though they could not make out the words. She died on the strand before morning, of the burns and of the cold, and the sexton of the graves nearest Arawn's door buried her with whatever it was still in her arms.

It was a statue, small enough to hold. What statue, and whose, the realm has three answers. Ariette, in the woods behind Fort Gwyntell, who wants it back and wants the girl freed, says it was a working of the old schools, a figure that held a magic of its own and would not let it go to anyone but the hand it was made for. The readers of Caer Gothwaite say it was only the school's household image, the little figure on the shelf by the door that the students touched for luck, and that the girl went back for it because nobody else would. The fishermen of Little Haven say she was singing to it.

When the witch called and Caldey stood up, Eralyne stood up with the rest, in the graveyard by the strand, with her arms still folded over the statue and her robe still scorched. She is a zombie now, and does what Morgana's dead do, and comes at anyone who walks among the graves; but the fishermen swear she still holds her arms that way. Ariette's errand is long, and goes through an apple tree's sap and a spirit that answers to it, and ends at this grave. The Gwyntell priests call it freeing. The fishermen call it taking the statue off her. Ariette says both are true.

The sexton stands a little way up the row from her, as he has since he buried her. When the living come in numbers, he comes down the row to her side.
legend: Eralyne is a level 55 zombie in the graveyard by the Caer Sidi strand on Caldey's west coast, the last step before the statue in Lost Treasure (Ariette, behind Fort Gwyntell: archiator hide, blue slime, Larionne's apple sap, the apple tree spirit, then Eralyne). She is aggressive from about 500 and an Undead Servant of Morgana; the Crypt Guardian (59) is about 600 off with the same faction, so a pair can take her alone but a bigger group can pull him in. No spells or styles in the data: a melee fight a duo or small group of fifties wins. Take the statue to Ariette and pick two different bracers. Respawn about 80 seconds.

loremasterTopic.text: A young student of the old schools of Avalon who went back into the burning school for a small statue and carried it, singing, on the last boat to [caldey], and died on the strand. The [crypt guardian] buried her with it in her arms. She stood up with the isle and holds it still. Ariette behind Fort Gwyntell wants it back and the girl freed; she says the two are the same.

bookPage: From the Ledger of Little Haven, kept by Mordwywr, enchanter. Paid: two silver to old Cadan, the last boatman still living who crossed on the night of the burning, for his account. He says the girl in the stern had her robe smoking and her arms round something and sang the whole way, a working-song of the schools, and did not stop when the boat grounded. He says he carried her up the strand himself and the sexton took her from him at the graves. I asked what she held. He said he did not look; you do not look at what a sorceress is holding. I have paid him for the account and not for that.
